messages:
olga: Heads up — started kernel 6.7.0 rollout to ap-southeast1 GPU hosts ~15m ago. Seeing a cluster of A100 nodes fail modprobe for nvidia module and then go NotReady.
josh: Can you paste the logs? which driver/kernel combo? any pattern by chassis or image?
olga: Quick snippet from one host:
```
Apr 12 10:07:42 host-433 kernel: nvidia: probe of 0000:3b:00.0 failed with error -22
Apr 12 10:07:42 host-433 kernel: nvidia: kernel module tainted
Apr 12 10:07:43 host-433 systemd: kubelet: NodeLease lost
```
infra-bot: alert: node host-433 evicted GPU workloads (OOM) — autotriggered drain
sean: NCCL handshakes also spiking on adjacent racks, seen timeouts 500-1000ms, some jobs falling back to CPU and increasing latency. Might be driver <-> kernel ABI mismatch.
maria: This is only ap-southeast1 canary pool, right? Any impact on Dedicated reserved capacity customers in that region?
olga: Mostly canary and some autoscaled Dedicated nodes. Two Dedicated pools in ap-southeast1 lost ~6 workers each. Customers on reserved capacity are impacted briefly as jobs get requeued.
josh: Ops options:
- pause kernel rollout (recommended)
- rollback hosts to 5.15 image via bootctl (slow)
- force-driver-fallback to 510 legacy tree (could break other models)
We need to weigh cost of rollback vs letting autoscaler spin new hosts (cost spike).
oncall: I'm leaning to pausing rollout and draining rest of the canary hosts. If we let autoscaler create replacements, we risk exhausting spare quota and run up GPU cloud cost.
infra-bot: action_log: rolled back kernel rollout flag for ap-southeast1 at 10:33 UTC; draining 8 hosts initiated.
deploy-bot: canary-rollout: paused by infra-bot (reason: module probe failures), timestamp 10:33 UTC
sean: For mitigation we can also patch the module probe logic to retry with delayed firmware load, but that's code change and risky for today.
maria: Notifying impacted customers: I can draft an advisory for reserved capacity customers in ap-southeast1. Recommend temporary routing to eu-west2 for latency-tolerant jobs.
josh: Also suggest adding a quick kernel-pin option in provisioning to pin instances to kernel 5.15 for Dedicated until we validate 6.7. That reduces blast radius.
olga: Agreed. Action items:
- @sean and @josh investigate modprobe root cause and test a driver build on a held host (ETA 2h)
- @maria prepare customer advisory and re-routing playbook (ETA 30m)
- @oncall observe autoscaler and hold any scale-ups that would exceed budget (ETA immediate)
- infra to mark images with compatibility metadata so provisioning can avoid 6.7 until verified
oncall: I'll also create a short runbook step to exclude hosts with the 6.7 kernel from scheduler labels.
josh: FYI: cost tradeoff estimate — rolling rollback for 200 hosts ~ $Xk/day extra vs risk of SLA credits if we let failures continue. Need signoff if rollback required at scale.
maria: I'll loop in finance/ops for the emergency spend approval if we need mass reprovisioning.
olga: Thanks all. Please post updates here. :eyes:
